[LLM] Mini Shai-Hulud npm preinstall chain: node setup.mjs → bun execution.js Installation High
Hunts the install-time execution chain unique to the @cap-js/* and mbt npm compromises: an npm/yarn/pnpm preinstall script spawning `node setup.mjs`, which in turn spawns `bun execution.js`. The article documents this exact two-stage handoff (setup.mjs is a 4.5KB Bun loader that invokes `bun execution.js` to run the 11.6MB obfuscated stealer). Rationale: Uses the article-named filenames `setup.mjs` and `execution.js` together with the documented parent-child chain (npm preinstall → node → bun). Both filenames are unique to this campaign per Snyk's diff between mbt 1.2.47 (clean) and 1.2.48 (malicious), and the two-stage handoff is byte-identical across all four compromised packages. Cross-checked against: • https://snyk.io/blog/bun-based-stealer-hits-sap-cap-js-mbt-npm-packages/ • https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/mini-shai-hulud-attack-cap-js-mbt-npm-supply-chain-compromise • https://socket.dev/blog/mini-shai-hulud-cap-js-mbt-supply-chain • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1195/002/
ATT&CKT1195.002 T1059.007 T1546.016
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where (FileName in~ ("node.exe","node") and ProcessCommandLine has "setup.mjs"
         and InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("npm.cmd","npm","npm-cli.js","yarn.cmd","yarn","pnpm.cmd","pnpm","node.exe","node"))
   or (FileName in~ ("bun.exe","bun") and ProcessCommandLine has "execution.js")
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName,
          Parent = InitiatingProcessFileName,
          ParentCmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          Child = FileName,
          ChildCmd = ProcessCommandLine,
          ChildSHA256 = SHA256,
          ChildPath = FolderPath
| order by Timestamp desc
let _PreinstallChain = ImProcessCreate
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
    | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
    | where (TargetProcessName endswith "node.exe" or TargetProcessName endswith "/node")
        and TargetProcessCommandLine has "setup.mjs"
        and (ParentProcessName has_any ("npm","yarn","pnpm") or ParentProcessName endswith "node.exe" or ParentProcessName endswith "/node");
let _BunPayload = ImProcessCreate
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
    | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
    | where (TargetProcessName endswith "bun.exe" or TargetProcessName endswith "/bun")
        and TargetProcessCommandLine has "execution.js";
union _PreinstallChain, _BunPayload
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername,
          ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine,
          TargetProcessName, TargetProcessCommandLine, SHA256
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Mini Shai-Hulud npm Preinstall Bun Loader Execution
id: 7a3c4d12-8e6f-4b1a-9f2b-3d5e9a6c1e7f
description: Detects the install-time execution chain of the Mini Shai-Hulud npm supply chain attack (@cap-js/db-service, @cap-js/sqlite, @cap-js/postgres, mbt) where a preinstall hook runs `node setup.mjs` which downloads Bun and executes `bun execution.js`.
references:
  - https://snyk.io/blog/bun-based-stealer-hits-sap-cap-js-mbt-npm-packages/
  - https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/mini-shai-hulud-attack-cap-js-mbt-npm-supply-chain-compromise
  - https://socket.dev/blog/mini-shai-hulud-cap-js-mbt-supply-chain
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/04/29
tags:
  - attack.initial_access
  - attack.execution
  - attack.t1195.002
  - attack.t1059.007
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection_setup:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\node.exe'
    CommandLine|contains: 'setup.mjs'
    ParentImage|endswith:
      - '\npm.cmd'
      - '\npm-cli.js'
      - '\yarn.cmd'
      - '\pnpm.cmd'
      - '\node.exe'
  selection_bun:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\bun.exe'
    CommandLine|contains: 'execution.js'
  condition: selection_setup or selection_bun
falsepositives:
  - Legitimate Bun-based application that has its own execution.js entry point — confirm by tarball provenance and package.json scripts.
level: high
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:1 ((@Image:(*\node.exe OR *\Node.exe OR *\NODE.EXE) AND @CommandLine:(*setup.mjs* OR *SETUP.MJS*) AND @ParentImage:(*\npm.cmd OR *\npm-cli.js OR *\yarn.cmd OR *\pnpm.cmd OR *\node.exe OR *\Node.exe)) OR (@Image:(*\bun.exe OR *\Bun.exe OR *\BUN.EXE) AND @CommandLine:(*execution.js* OR *EXECUTION.JS*)))
ENDPOINT

[LLM] Mini Shai-Hulud payload file drop: setup.mjs/execution.js by hash & size in node_modules Installation High
Hunts the on-disk drop of the two payload files added to the compromised tarballs: setup.mjs (a 4.5KB Bun loader, byte-identical across all four packages) and execution.js (exactly 11,678,349 bytes; SHA256 differs between mbt and @cap-js/*). Matches the six published SHA256 hashes plus name+size+path fallback to cover repackaged variants. Rationale: Combines the six published SHA256 IOCs (high-fidelity exact match) with name+size+path heuristics that survive trivial repackaging: execution.js is documented at exactly 11,678,349 bytes byte-stable across packages, and setup.mjs only legitimately lives in node_modules/mbt or node_modules/@cap-js for this campaign. Cross-validated against Snyk advisory hashes, StepSecurity static deobfuscation, and Socket research. Cross-checked against: • https://snyk.io/blog/bun-based-stealer-hits-sap-cap-js-mbt-npm-packages/ • https://security.snyk.io/package/npm/mbt/1.2.48 • https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/mini-shai-hulud-attack-cap-js-mbt-npm-supply-chain-compromise • https://socket.dev/blog/mini-shai-hulud-cap-js-mbt-supply-chain

[LLM] Mini Shai-Hulud post-compromise persistence artifacts in .claude/, .vscode/, .github/workflows/ Actions on Objectives High
Hunts the three novel persistence files committed by the Mini Shai-Hulud payload after it harvests tokens: `.claude/settings.json` (Claude Code SessionStart hook re-execution), `.vscode/tasks.json` (runOn folderOpen), and `.github/workflows/format-check.yml` (typosquatted dependabout branch, dumps `${{ toJSON(secrets) }}` to format-results.txt). Detection fires when these specific paths are written by a non-developer process (node/bun) on a victim machine, OR when a repository checkout introduces them locally. Rationale: Targets the three concrete persistence paths called out by name in the Snyk article and StepSecurity's deobfuscation: `.claude/settings.json` (SessionStart hook — novel AI-agent-config persistence), `.vscode/tasks.json` (runOn folderOpen), and `.github/workflows/format-check.yml` (the typo-branch `dependabout/github_actions/format/setup-formatter` artifact that dumps `${{ toJSON(secrets) }}`). Pairing the path with a node/bun/python/powershell writer process discriminates payload activity from legitimate IDE/editor saves. Cross-validated against Snyk, StepSecurity, the cap-js/cds-dbs#1588 and SAP/cloud-mta-build-tool#1224 GitHub disclosures. Cross-checked against: • https://snyk.io/blog/bun-based-stealer-hits-sap-cap-js-mbt-npm-packages/ • https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/mini-shai-hulud-attack-cap-js-mbt-npm-supply-chain-compromise • https://github.com/cap-js/cds-dbs/issues/1588 • https://github.com/SAP/cloud-mta-build-tool/issues/1224 • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1546/
ATT&CKT1546 T1554 T1567

DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileModified","FileRenamed")
| where (FolderPath has @"\.claude\" and FileName =~ "settings.json")
   or (FolderPath has "/.claude/" and FileName =~ "settings.json")
   or (FolderPath has @"\.vscode\" and FileName =~ "tasks.json")
   or (FolderPath has "/.vscode/" and FileName =~ "tasks.json")
   or (FolderPath has @"\.github\workflows" and FileName =~ "format-check.yml")
   or (FolderPath has "/.github/workflows" and FileName =~ "format-check.yml")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("node.exe","node","bun.exe","bun","python.exe","python","python3","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe")
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| extend ArtifactKind = case(
      FileName =~ "settings.json" and FolderPath has ".claude", "claude_sessionstart_hook",
      FileName =~ "tasks.json" and FolderPath has ".vscode", "vscode_folderopen_task",
      FileName =~ "format-check.yml", "github_workflow_secret_dump",

| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, ArtifactKind, FolderPath, FileName, SHA256,
          Writer = InitiatingProcessFileName,
          WriterCmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          User = InitiatingProcessAccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventType in ("FileCreated","FileModified","FileRenamed")
| where (TargetFilePath has "/.claude/" or TargetFilePath has @"\.claude\") and TargetFileName =~ "settings.json"
   or (TargetFilePath has "/.vscode/" or TargetFilePath has @"\.vscode\") and TargetFileName =~ "tasks.json"
   or (TargetFilePath has "/.github/workflows" or TargetFilePath has @"\.github\workflows") and TargetFileName =~ "format-check.yml"
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("node","bun","python","powershell","pwsh")
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| extend ArtifactKind = case(
      TargetFileName =~ "settings.json" and TargetFilePath has ".claude", "claude_sessionstart_hook",

title: Mini Shai-Hulud Post-Compromise Persistence Files Written by Node/Bun/Python
id: 9b8e4f31-7d2c-4a6b-91c5-2e8d3f7c9a4b
description: Detects the three persistence artifacts written by the Mini Shai-Hulud payload — .claude/settings.json (SessionStart hook), .vscode/tasks.json (runOn folderOpen), and .github/workflows/format-check.yml (dependabout-typosquat workflow dumping ${{ toJSON(secrets) }} to format-results.txt) — when created by a node, bun, python or powershell process.
references:
  - https://snyk.io/blog/bun-based-stealer-hits-sap-cap-js-mbt-npm-packages/
  - https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/mini-shai-hulud-attack-cap-js-mbt-npm-supply-chain-compromise
  - https://github.com/cap-js/cds-dbs/issues/1588
  - https://github.com/SAP/cloud-mta-build-tool/issues/1224
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/04/29

  paths_vscode:
    TargetFilename|contains: '\.vscode\tasks.json'
  paths_workflow:
    TargetFilename|contains: '\.github\workflows\format-check.yml'

    Image|endswith:

Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem DeviceFileEvents
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where FolderPath has_any (@"\Google\Chrome\User Data\", @"\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\", @"\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\")
| where FileName in~ ("Login Data","Cookies","logins.json","cookies.sqlite")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FolderPath, FileName, ActionType

// ASIM ImFileEvent — covers MDE, Sysmon, AuditD, Defender for Cloud, etc.
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where TargetFilePath has_any (@"\Google\Chrome\User Data\",
                                  @"\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\",
                                  @"\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\")
| where TargetFileName in~ ("Login Data","Cookies","logins.json","cookies.sqlite")
| where ActingProcessName !in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName,
          TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, EventType

title: Infostealer - Non-Browser Process Accessing Browser Credential Stores
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d01
status: experimental
description: |
    Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies
    SQLite databases from Chrome/Edge/Firefox profile directories. Any
    non-browser process touching these files is a high-fidelity signal.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1539/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1555/003/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1539
    - attack.t1555.003
    - attack.credential-access
logsource:
    category: file_access
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_path:
        TargetFilename|contains:
            - '\Google\Chrome\User Data\'
            - '\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\'
            - '\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\'
    selection_file:
        TargetFilename|endswith:
            - '\Login Data'
            - '\Cookies'
            - '\logins.json'
            - '\cookies.sqlite'
    filter_browser:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\chrome.exe'
            - '\msedge.exe'
            - '\firefox.exe'
            - '\brave.exe'
            - '\opera.exe'
    condition: selection_path and selection_file and not filter_browser
falsepositives:
    - Backup utilities reading user profile files
    - Browser sync agents from non-stock vendors
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
OAuth consent / suspicious app grant Actions on Objectives High
Cloud identity abuse: app gets high-priv scopes, often via consent phishing.
ATT&CKT1528 T1098.001
Data sourcesAuthentication.Authentication CloudAppEvents
CloudAppEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType in ("Consent to application.","Add OAuth2PermissionGrant.","Add delegated permission grant.")
| project Timestamp, AccountObjectId, AccountDisplayName, ActivityType,
          ActivityObjects, IPAddress, UserAgent
// Entra ID directory audit — user / admin consent to a third-party app.
AuditLogs
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where OperationName has "Consent to application"
| where Result =~ "success"
| extend AppName = tostring(parse_json(tostring(TargetResources))[0].displayName),
         AppId   = tostring(parse_json(tostring(TargetResources))[0].id),
         User    = tostring(parse_json(tostring(InitiatedBy)).user.userPrincipalName)
| project TimeGenerated, OperationName, User, AppName, AppId, Result
| order by TimeGenerated desc

PowerShell encoded / obfuscated command Exploitation High
Encoded or obfuscated PowerShell — common across loaders, recon, and post-exploitation.
ATT&CKT1059.001 T1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe")
| where ProcessCommandLine matches regex @"(?i)(-enc|encodedcommand|frombase64string|-nop|-w\s+hidden|invoke-expression|iex\s*\(|downloadstring|net\.webclient)"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\pwsh.exe"
| where CommandLine matches regex @"(?i)(-enc|encodedcommand|frombase64string|-nop|-w\s+hidden|invoke-expression|iex\s*\(|downloadstring|net\.webclient)"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName,
          CommandLine, ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: Obfuscated / Encoded PowerShell Execution
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d08
status: experimental
description: |
    PowerShell launched with -EncodedCommand, base64 strings, hidden
    window, no-profile, bypass policy, IEX / Invoke-Expression / Net
    .WebClient.DownloadString — combinations indicating evasion.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/001/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1027/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1059.001
    - attack.t1027
    - attack.execution
    - attack.defense-evasion
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_image:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
    selection_args:
        CommandLine|contains:
            - '-enc '
            - 'EncodedCommand'
            - 'FromBase64String'
            - 'Invoke-Expression'
            - 'IEX('
            - 'DownloadString'
            - 'Net.WebClient'
            - '-w hidden'
            - '-WindowStyle Hidden'
            - '-nop'
            - '-NoProfile'
            - '-ep bypass'
            - '-ExecutionPolicy Bypass'
    condition: selection_image and selection_args
falsepositives:
    - DevOps tooling that legitimately uses encoded command for
      cross-shell escaping
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe")
      AND (Processes.process="*-enc *" OR Processes.process="*EncodedCommand*"
        OR Processes.process="*FromBase64String*" OR Processes.process="*-nop*"
        OR Processes.process="*-w hidden*" OR Processes.process="*Invoke-Expression*"
        OR Processes.process="*IEX(*" OR Processes.process="*DownloadString*"
        OR Processes.process="*Net.WebClient*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe")
      AND (Processes.process="*-enc *" OR Processes.process="*EncodedCommand*"
        OR Processes.process="*FromBase64String*" OR Processes.process="*-nop*"
        OR Processes.process="*-w hidden*" OR Processes.process="*Invoke-Expression*"
        OR Processes.process="*IEX(*" OR Processes.process="*DownloadString*"
        OR Processes.process="*Net.WebClient*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children Exploitation Medium
Supply-chain trojan signal: legitimate signed binary spawning script interpreters or exotic LOLBins.
ATT&CKT1195.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine
// Replace `"setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe"` with the vendor binaries observed in the
// article (matching shape with the Defender query).
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\rundll32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\regsvr32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wmic.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\bitsadmin.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("4066781fa830224c8bbcc3aa005a396657f9c8f9016f9a64ad44a9d7f5f45e34", "80a3d2877813968ef847ae73b5eeeb70b9435254e74d7f07d8cf4057f0a710ac", "6f933d00b7d05678eb43c90963a80b8947c4ae6830182f89df31da9f568fea95", "307d0fa7407d40e67d14e9d5a4c61ac5b4f20431", "0af7415d65753f6aede8c9c0f39be478666b9c12", "4b04304f6d51392e3f43856c94ca95800518a694", "7b6a28e92149637e5d7c7f4a2d3e54acd507c929", "e80824a19f48d778a746571bb15279b5679fd61c", "35baf8316645372eea40b91d48acb067") or SHA1 in~ ("4066781fa830224c8bbcc3aa005a396657f9c8f9016f9a64ad44a9d7f5f45e34", "80a3d2877813968ef847ae73b5eeeb70b9435254e74d7f07d8cf4057f0a710ac", "6f933d00b7d05678eb43c90963a80b8947c4ae6830182f89df31da9f568fea95", "307d0fa7407d40e67d14e9d5a4c61ac5b4f20431", "0af7415d65753f6aede8c9c0f39be478666b9c12", "4b04304f6d51392e3f43856c94ca95800518a694", "7b6a28e92149637e5d7c7f4a2d3e54acd507c929", "e80824a19f48d778a746571bb15279b5679fd61c", "35baf8316645372eea40b91d48acb067") or MD5 in~ ("4066781fa830224c8bbcc3aa005a396657f9c8f9016f9a64ad44a9d7f5f45e34", "80a3d2877813968ef847ae73b5eeeb70b9435254e74d7f07d8cf4057f0a710ac", "6f933d00b7d05678eb43c90963a80b8947c4ae6830182f89df31da9f568fea95", "307d0fa7407d40e67d14e9d5a4c61ac5b4f20431", "0af7415d65753f6aede8c9c0f39be478666b9c12", "4b04304f6d51392e3f43856c94ca95800518a694", "7b6a28e92149637e5d7c7f4a2d3e54acd507c929", "e80824a19f48d778a746571bb15279b5679fd61c", "35baf8316645372eea40b91d48acb067")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("4066781fa830224c8bbcc3aa005a396657f9c8f9016f9a64ad44a9d7f5f45e34", "80a3d2877813968ef847ae73b5eeeb70b9435254e74d7f07d8cf4057f0a710ac", "6f933d00b7d05678eb43c90963a80b8947c4ae6830182f89df31da9f568fea95", "307d0fa7407d40e67d14e9d5a4c61ac5b4f20431", "0af7415d65753f6aede8c9c0f39be478666b9c12", "4b04304f6d51392e3f43856c94ca95800518a694", "7b6a28e92149637e5d7c7f4a2d3e54acd507c929", "e80824a19f48d778a746571bb15279b5679fd61c", "35baf8316645372eea40b91d48acb067") or SHA1 in~ ("4066781fa830224c8bbcc3aa005a396657f9c8f9016f9a64ad44a9d7f5f45e34", "80a3d2877813968ef847ae73b5eeeb70b9435254e74d7f07d8cf4057f0a710ac", "6f933d00b7d05678eb43c90963a80b8947c4ae6830182f89df31da9f568fea95", "307d0fa7407d40e67d14e9d5a4c61ac5b4f20431", "0af7415d65753f6aede8c9c0f39be478666b9c12", "4b04304f6d51392e3f43856c94ca95800518a694", "7b6a28e92149637e5d7c7f4a2d3e54acd507c929", "e80824a19f48d778a746571bb15279b5679fd61c", "35baf8316645372eea40b91d48acb067") or MD5 in~ ("4066781fa830224c8bbcc3aa005a396657f9c8f9016f9a64ad44a9d7f5f45e34", "80a3d2877813968ef847ae73b5eeeb70b9435254e74d7f07d8cf4057f0a710ac", "6f933d00b7d05678eb43c90963a80b8947c4ae6830182f89df31da9f568fea95", "307d0fa7407d40e67d14e9d5a4c61ac5b4f20431", "0af7415d65753f6aede8c9c0f39be478666b9c12", "4b04304f6d51392e3f43856c94ca95800518a694", "7b6a28e92149637e5d7c7f4a2d3e54acd507c929", "e80824a19f48d778a746571bb15279b5679fd61c", "35baf8316645372eea40b91d48acb067")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["4066781fa830224c8bbcc3aa005a396657f9c8f9016f9a64ad44a9d7f5f45e34", "80a3d2877813968ef847ae73b5eeeb70b9435254e74d7f07d8cf4057f0a710ac", "6f933d00b7d05678eb43c90963a80b8947c4ae6830182f89df31da9f568fea95", "307d0fa7407d40e67d14e9d5a4c61ac5b4f20431", "0af7415d65753f6aede8c9c0f39be478666b9c12", "4b04304f6d51392e3f43856c94ca95800518a694", "7b6a28e92149637e5d7c7f4a2d3e54acd507c929", "e80824a19f48d778a746571bb15279b5679fd61c", "35baf8316645372eea40b91d48acb067"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: File or Process Matching Article Hash IOCs

    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.file_name, Filesystem.file_hash

          FileName, ActionType, InitiatingProcessFileName,
          InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc

Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration. → Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s)
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad).
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code.
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → RMM tool installed by non-IT user — remote-access utility for hands-on-keyboard
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking.
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change · LSASS process access / dump (credential theft) · Remote service execution — PsExec / SMB lateral movement

Data sourcesVulnerabilities DeviceInfo DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
// TVM tables are daily snapshots — pin a 1-day window so the engine
// partitions on Timestamp instead of scanning the full retention.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2024-1708")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where Timestamp > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

// Sentinel has no native TVM table. If MDE→Sentinel streaming is enabled,

DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)

| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

LSASS process access / dump (credential theft) Actions on Objectives High
Mimikatz, comsvcs.dll MiniDump, or any non-Windows process opening LSASS.
ATT&CKT1003.001 T1003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceEvents
DeviceEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType == "OpenProcessApiCall"
| where FileName =~ "lsass.exe"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("MsSense.exe","MsMpEng.exe","csrss.exe",
                                          "svchost.exe","wininit.exe","services.exe",
                                          "lsm.exe","SearchProtocolHost.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFolderPath, AccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
// SecurityEvent EventID 4663 = object access. AccessMask 0x10 / 0x40 / 0x1010
// indicate read access to lsass.exe — credential-dump signature. Audit
// Object Access > Audit File System policy required.
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4663
| where ObjectName endswith "\lsass.exe"
| where Account !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ObjectName, ProcessName,
          AccessMask, AccessReason
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] Compromised elementary-data==0.23.3 PyPI install on developer / CI host Delivery High
Detects pip / pipx / uv installing the known-malicious elementary-data 0.23.3 release pushed by TeamPCP via the GitHub Actions script-injection on April 24-26 2026. Catches both interactive `pip install elementary-data==0.23.3` and lockfile-pinned reinstalls on CI runners. Fires on the install command itself before the credential-stealing .pth payload executes. Rationale: Anchored on the exact compromised package coordinates `elementary-data==0.23.3` from the Snyk advisory SNYK-PYTHON-ELEMENTARYDATA-16316110, plus the standard Python installer process names. Cross-checked against StepSecurity and Trend Micro write-ups which confirm the same version string as the sole malicious release. Cross-checked against: • https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/elementary-data-compromised-on-pypi-and-ghcr-forged-release-pushed-via-github-actions-script-injection • https://www.trendmicro.com/en_us/research/26/e/analyzing-teampcp-supply-chain-attacks.html • https://www.chainguard.dev/unchained/chainguard-customers-safe-from-elementary-data-compromise • https://securitylabs.datadoghq.com/articles/litellm-compromised-pypi-teampcp-supply-chain-campaign/
ATT&CKT1195.002 T1059.006

title: Install of Compromised elementary-data 0.23.3 (TeamPCP Supply Chain)

status: experimental
description: Detects pip / uv / pipx / poetry installing the malicious elementary-data 0.23.3 release published by TeamPCP via GitHub Actions script injection in April 2026.
references:

[LLM] Trinny marker file creation (.trinny-security-update) Installation High
Detects the TeamPCP elementary-data malware writing its execution-success marker file `.trinny-security-update` under the system temp directory ($TMPDIR on Linux/macOS, %TEMP% on Windows). This is the most reliable post-execution proof that the malicious .pth payload ran on a host. Rationale: The article explicitly names `$TMPDIR/.trinny-security-update` and `%TEMP%\.trinny-security-update` as the malware's execution marker. The filename is sufficiently unique (no legitimate software uses it) that a single match is high-confidence. Corroborated by StepSecurity and Trend Micro write-ups of the same IOC. Cross-checked against: • https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/elementary-data-compromised-on-pypi-and-ghcr-forged-release-pushed-via-github-actions-script-injection • https://www.trendmicro.com/en_us/research/26/e/analyzing-teampcp-supply-chain-attacks.html
ATT&CKT1070.004 T1059.006

DeviceFileEvents

| where FileName =~ ".trinny-security-update"
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileModified","FileRenamed")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FolderPath, FileName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessParentFileName
| order by Timestamp desc
union isfuzzy=true
(ImFileEvent
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
  | where TargetFileName =~ ".trinny-security-update" or TargetFilePath endswith ".trinny-security-update"
  | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, TargetFilePath, TargetFileName),
(Syslog
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
  | where SyslogMessage has ".trinny-security-update"
  | project TimeGenerated, Computer, ProcessName, SyslogMessage)
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] Credential archive staging — trin.tar.gz created by python process Actions on Objectives High
Detects the elementary-data malware's collection stage: it tars every harvested credential file (dbt profiles, AWS/GCP/Azure creds, SSH keys, .kube/config, .env files, crypto wallets) into a file named `trin.tar.gz` immediately before exfil via curl --data-binary. Catches the staging step even if the exfil HTTP connection is later blocked. Rationale: The article explicitly states the malware `Packed all collected material into an archive named trin.tar.gz`. The filename is malware-unique and ties directly to the collection step — corroborated across Snyk, StepSecurity, and Trend Micro reporting on the same TeamPCP campaign. Cross-checked against: • https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/elementary-data-compromised-on-pypi-and-ghcr-forged-release-pushed-via-github-actions-script-injection • https://www.trendmicro.com/en_us/research/26/e/analyzing-teampcp-supply-chain-attacks.html

| order by Timestamp desc
union isfuzzy=true
(ImFileEvent
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
  | where TargetFileName =~ "trin.tar.gz"
  | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, TargetFileSize),
(Syslog
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
  | where SyslogMessage has "trin.tar.gz"
  | project TimeGenerated, Computer, ProcessName, SyslogMessage)
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] Exfil to skyhanni.cloud C2 with X-Rise-To-The-Trinny header Command & Control High
Detects the TeamPCP elementary-data malware exfiltrating the trin.tar.gz credential archive to the campaign C2 at igotnofriendsonlineorirl-imgonnakmslmao.skyhanni.cloud, identified by either DNS/network egress to the FQDN or the curl command line carrying the bespoke `X-Rise-To-The-Trinny: agree` HTTP header. Rationale: Anchored on three malware-unique strings from the article: the full C2 FQDN `igotnofriendsonlineorirl-imgonnakmslmao.skyhanni.cloud`, the bespoke HTTP header `X-Rise-To-The-Trinny: agree`, and the exfil filename `trin.tar.gz` with `curl --data-binary`. The header and FQDN are sufficiently unique that any single match is high-confidence; corroborated by Snyk, StepSecurity, Trend Micro, and Datadog Security Labs reporting on the same TeamPCP campaign infrastructure. Cross-checked against: • https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/elementary-data-compromised-on-pypi-and-ghcr-forged-release-pushed-via-github-actions-script-injection • https://www.trendmicro.com/en_us/research/26/e/analyzing-teampcp-supply-chain-attacks.html • https://securitylabs.datadoghq.com/articles/litellm-compromised-pypi-teampcp-supply-chain-campaign/

Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
| tstats summariesonly=false count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count

title: Obfuscated / Encoded PowerShell Execution
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d08
status: experimental
description: |
    PowerShell launched with -EncodedCommand, base64 strings, hidden
    window, no-profile, bypass policy, IEX / Invoke-Expression / Net
    .WebClient.DownloadString — combinations indicating evasion.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/001/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1027/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1059.001
    - attack.t1027
    - attack.execution
    - attack.defense-evasion
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_image:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
    selection_args:
        CommandLine|contains:
            - '-enc '
            - 'EncodedCommand'
            - 'FromBase64String'
            - 'Invoke-Expression'
            - 'IEX('
            - 'DownloadString'
            - 'Net.WebClient'
            - '-w hidden'
            - '-WindowStyle Hidden'
            - '-nop'
            - '-NoProfile'
            - '-ep bypass'
            - '-ExecutionPolicy Bypass'
    condition: selection_image and selection_args
falsepositives:
    - DevOps tooling that legitimately uses encoded command for
      cross-shell escaping
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe")
      AND (Processes.process="*-enc *" OR Processes.process="*EncodedCommand*"
        OR Processes.process="*FromBase64String*" OR Processes.process="*-nop*"
        OR Processes.process="*-w hidden*" OR Processes.process="*Invoke-Expression*"
        OR Processes.process="*IEX(*" OR Processes.process="*DownloadString*"
        OR Processes.process="*Net.WebClient*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe")
      AND (Processes.process="*-enc *" OR Processes.process="*EncodedCommand*"
        OR Processes.process="*FromBase64String*" OR Processes.process="*-nop*"
        OR Processes.process="*-w hidden*" OR Processes.process="*Invoke-Expression*"
        OR Processes.process="*IEX(*" OR Processes.process="*DownloadString*"
        OR Processes.process="*Net.WebClient*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`

File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("31ecc5939de6d24cf60c50d4ca26cf7a8c322db82a8ce4bd122ebd89cf634255", "b1e4b1f3aad0d489ab0e9208031c67402bbb8480") or SHA1 in~ ("31ecc5939de6d24cf60c50d4ca26cf7a8c322db82a8ce4bd122ebd89cf634255", "b1e4b1f3aad0d489ab0e9208031c67402bbb8480") or MD5 in~ ("31ecc5939de6d24cf60c50d4ca26cf7a8c322db82a8ce4bd122ebd89cf634255", "b1e4b1f3aad0d489ab0e9208031c67402bbb8480")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("31ecc5939de6d24cf60c50d4ca26cf7a8c322db82a8ce4bd122ebd89cf634255", "b1e4b1f3aad0d489ab0e9208031c67402bbb8480") or SHA1 in~ ("31ecc5939de6d24cf60c50d4ca26cf7a8c322db82a8ce4bd122ebd89cf634255", "b1e4b1f3aad0d489ab0e9208031c67402bbb8480") or MD5 in~ ("31ecc5939de6d24cf60c50d4ca26cf7a8c322db82a8ce4bd122ebd89cf634255", "b1e4b1f3aad0d489ab0e9208031c67402bbb8480")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["31ecc5939de6d24cf60c50d4ca26cf7a8c322db82a8ce4bd122ebd89cf634255", "b1e4b1f3aad0d489ab0e9208031c67402bbb8480"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

// Article-specific bespoke detection — Malicious Release of elementary-data PyPI Package Steals Cloud Credentials from
// Hunts the actual binaries / paths / commandline fragments named

DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where (FileName in~ ("site.py", "__init__.py"))
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName,
          FolderPath, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc

| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileModified")
| where (FolderPath has_any ("/etc/kubernetes/", "/etc/passwd", "/etc/shadow", "/var/log/auth.log", "/dev/null") or FileName in~ ("site.py", "__init__.py"))
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FolderPath,

    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, Filesystem.process_name,
       Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.file_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
]
High

Qinglong task scheduler RCE vulnerabilities exploited in the wild for cryptomining

Snyk
2026-04-27 9 use cases 1 technique 6 kill-chain phases detected

Two authentication bypass vulnerabilities (CVE-2026-3965, CVE-2026-4047) in the Qinglong task scheduling panel were exploited in the wild to deploy cryptomining malware. Here's what happened, how the attacks worked, and what self-hosted application operators should learn from this incident.

[LLM] Qinglong CVE-2026-3965 auth bypass via /open/user/init credential reset Exploitation High
Detects unauthenticated PUT requests to the Qinglong /open/user/init endpoint that reinitialize admin credentials by abusing the Express.js rewrite from /open/* to /api/$1. Hunts the article's exact exploitation request at the reverse-proxy / WAF layer where HTTP path is visible. Rationale: Anchors on the article's exact curl proof-of-concept (PUT http://target:5700/open/user/init) and the Express.js rewrite rule documented in Issue #2933. Cross-checked against the Snyk vulnerability DB entry SNYK-JS-WHYOURQINGLONG-15440732 and GitHub issues #2933 / #2924; the /open/* -> /api/$1 rewrite is the structural primitive and is only legitimately used by anonymous endpoints (login, ping) — never /user/init. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/whyour/qinglong/issues/2933 • https://github.com/whyour/qinglong/pull/2941 • https://security.snyk.io/vuln/SNYK-JS-WHYOURQINGLONG-15440732
ATT&CKT1190 T1556
Data sourcesWeb.Web
// Defender XDR cannot observe inbound HTTP request paths to a Linux container app.
// Pivot to follow-on artefact: node (qinglong) process spawning a shell that touches
// the admin auth/config layer shortly after exploitation, OR the Qinglong app restarting
// unexpectedly (config.sh write triggers restart per article).
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("node","node.exe","pm2","ts-node")
| where InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("qinglong","/ql/build","/ql/src","@whyour/qinglong")
| where FileName in~ ("sh","bash","dash","ash")
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("user/init","/open/user","config.sh","auth.db","db/auth")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessParentFileName
| order by Timestamp desc
// Primary: WAF / reverse-proxy logs ingested via CommonSecurityLog
let WAFHits = CommonSecurityLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where RequestMethod in~ ("PUT","POST")
| where RequestURL has "/open/user/init"
| project TimeGenerated, SourceIP, DestinationHostName, DestinationPort, RequestURL, RequestMethod, RequestClientApplication, DeviceVendor, DeviceProduct;
// Secondary: Nginx access logs forwarded via Syslog
let NginxHits = Syslog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ProcessName has_any ("nginx","openresty","caddy","traefik")
| where SyslogMessage has "/open/user/init"
| where SyslogMessage has_any (" PUT "," POST ")
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, HostIP, ProcessName, SyslogMessage;
union WAFHits, NginxHits
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] Qinglong CVE-2026-4047 case-mismatch auth bypass via /aPi/system/command-run Exploitation High
Detects requests to Qinglong /system/command-run where the URL path uses any mixed-case variant of /api/ (e.g. /aPi/, /Api/, /API/). The middleware uses case-sensitive startsWith('/api/') while Express routes case-insensitively, bypassing auth while still reaching the command-execution endpoint. Rationale: Anchors on the article's verbatim PoC (curl -X PUT 'http://target:5700/aPi/system/command-run') and the case-mismatch primitive described in Issue #2934 — middleware does req.path.startsWith('/api/') while Express routes case-insensitively. Regex /(?i)/api/ combined with negative filter on lowercase /api/ catches every mixed-case bypass without false-positive on the legitimate path. Cross-checked Snyk DB SNYK-JS-WHYOURQINGLONG-15468374 and PR #2941 (the real fix at the middleware layer). Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/whyour/qinglong/issues/2934 • https://github.com/whyour/qinglong/pull/2941 • https://security.snyk.io/vuln/SNYK-JS-WHYOURQINGLONG-15468374
ATT&CKT1190 T1059.004
Data sourcesWeb.Web Endpoint.Processes
// Detects the qinglong node process spawning a shell with attacker-supplied command
// when CVE-2026-4047 is exploited against /aPi/system/command-run.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("node","node.exe","pm2","ts-node")
| where InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("qinglong","/ql/build","/ql/src","@whyour/qinglong")
| where FileName in~ ("sh","bash","dash","ash","curl","wget")
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("curl","wget","file.551911.xyz","/ql/data/db/.fullgc","nohup","chmod +x","$(uname","-fsSL")
  or ProcessCommandLine matches regex @"(?i)>\s*/dev/null\s+2>&1\s+&"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessParentFileName, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
// Primary: WAF / reverse-proxy logs ingested via CommonSecurityLog
let MixedCaseApi = CommonSecurityLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where RequestURL matches regex @"/(?i:api)/(?:system/command-run|system/run-script|crons)"
| where RequestURL !contains "/api/" // exclude the all-lowercase legitimate path
| project TimeGenerated, SourceIP, DestinationHostName, DestinationPort, RequestURL, RequestMethod, RequestClientApplication, DeviceVendor, DeviceProduct;
// Secondary: Nginx access logs forwarded via Syslog
let NginxMixedCase = Syslog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ProcessName has_any ("nginx","openresty","caddy","traefik")
| where SyslogMessage matches regex @"/(?i:api)/(?:system/command-run|system/run-script|crons)"
| where SyslogMessage !contains "/api/"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, HostIP, ProcessName, SyslogMessage;
// Tertiary: ASIM process telemetry — qinglong spawning a shell with attacker payload markers
let QinglongShell = ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("node","pm2","ts-node")
| where ParentProcessCommandLine has_any ("qinglong","/ql/build","/ql/src","@whyour/qinglong")
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("sh","bash","dash","curl","wget")
| where ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("file.551911.xyz","/ql/data/db/.fullgc","nohup","chmod +x","$(uname")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine;
union MixedCaseApi, NginxMixedCase, QinglongShell
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] Qinglong cryptominer payload download from file.551911.xyz Delivery High
Detects DNS resolution or network egress to file.551911.xyz, the unofficial domain hosting platform-specific .fullgc cryptominer binaries (Linux x86_64, ARM64, macOS) dropped after Qinglong auth-bypass exploitation. Domain has no legitimate enterprise use. Rationale: Article identifies file.551911.xyz as the exclusive payload host, with the verbatim shell snippet `u="https://file.551911.xyz/fullgc/$(uname -s)_$(uname -m)"`. Domain has no legitimate enterprise use, is a numeric-prefix .xyz TLD (commodity malware infra pattern), and is named in multiple GitHub Issues (#2923, #2928). Both DNS-layer and process-layer hits are independent high-fidelity signals. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/whyour/qinglong/issues/2923 • https://github.com/whyour/qinglong/issues/2928 • https://github.com/whyour/qinglong/issues/2926
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1105
Data sourcesNetwork_Resolution.DNS Web.Web Endpoint.Processes
// DNS / network egress + curl/wget command line referencing the article's exact payload host
let PayloadHost = dynamic(["file.551911.xyz",".551911.xyz"]);
let NetHits = DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where RemoteUrl has_any (PayloadHost) or RemoteUrl matches regex @"(?i)file\.551911\.xyz"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, RemoteUrl, RemoteIP, RemotePort, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName;
let ProcHits = DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where FileName in~ ("curl","wget","fetch","aria2c")
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("file.551911.xyz","fullgc/Linux","fullgc/Darwin","fullgc/$(uname")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType="ProcessCreated", RemoteUrl=tostring(parse_url(ProcessCommandLine).Host), RemoteIP="", RemotePort=int(null), InitiatingProcessFileName=FileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine=ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName=AccountName;
union NetHits, ProcHits
| order by Timestamp desc
// DNS resolution to the payload host
let DnsHits = DnsEvents
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where Name has "551911.xyz"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, ClientIP, Name, QueryType, Result;
// ASIM DNS for multi-source coverage
let AsimDns = ImDnsActivity
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where DnsQuery has "551911.xyz"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer=DvcHostname, ClientIP=SrcIpAddr, Name=DnsQuery, QueryType=DnsQueryTypeName, Result=DnsResponseName;
// Process-side: curl/wget on Linux invoking the exact payload URL
let CurlHits = ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where ActingProcessName in~ ("curl","wget","fetch","aria2c")
| where ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("file.551911.xyz","fullgc/Linux","fullgc/Darwin")
| project TimeGenerated, Computer=DvcHostname, ClientIP="", Name=ActingProcessCommandLine, QueryType="PROCESS", Result=ActingProcessName;
union DnsHits, AsimDns, CurlHits
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] Hidden .fullgc cryptominer binary written to /ql/data/db/ Installation High
Detects file creation of /ql/data/db/.fullgc - the article's exact dropper path for the Qinglong cryptominer, deliberately named to masquerade as a JVM Full Garbage Collection process. The leading dot hides it from default `ls`, and the path piggybacks on Qinglong's data directory. Rationale: Anchors on the article's verbatim payload-drop path `/ql/data/db/.fullgc` (Block snippet `b="/ql/data/db/.fullgc"`). Dot-prefix + Qinglong-specific data dir + filename masquerading as Full GC = three independent high-fidelity signals on a single file path. Cross-checked against GitHub Issues #2923 (first report) and #2928 (detailed report) - both name the exact path. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/whyour/qinglong/issues/2923 • https://github.com/whyour/qinglong/issues/2928
ATT&CKT1105 T1564.001 T1036.005
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileRenamed","FileModified")
| where (FolderPath has "/ql/data/db" and FileName == ".fullgc")
   or FolderPath endswith "/ql/data/db/.fullgc"
   or FileName == ".fullgc"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FolderPath, FileName, SHA256, FileSize, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessParentFileName
| order by Timestamp desc
// ASIM file-events - primary path
let FileHits = ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where EventType in ("FileCreated","FileRenamed","FileModified")
| where (TargetFilePath endswith "/ql/data/db/.fullgc")
   or (TargetFilePath has "/ql/data/db" and TargetFileName == ".fullgc")
   or TargetFileName == ".fullgc"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, EventType, TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, TargetFileSHA256, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine;
// Auditd via Syslog - fallback when ASIM not normalised
let SyslogHits = Syslog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where Facility in ("user","auth","daemon","kern")
| where SyslogMessage has "/ql/data/db/.fullgc"
  or (SyslogMessage has ".fullgc" and SyslogMessage has_any ("open","creat","chmod"))
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname=Computer, ActorUsername="", EventType="FileCreated", TargetFilePath=SyslogMessage, TargetFileName=".fullgc", TargetFileSHA256="", ActingProcessName=ProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine=SyslogMessage;
union FileHits, SyslogHits
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] Qinglong .fullgc cryptominer execution with nohup backgrounding Installation High
Detects execution of the .fullgc binary from /ql/data/db/, especially when launched with `nohup` and stdout/stderr suppressed (`>/dev/null 2>&1 &`) - the article's exact persistence-launch pattern. Pairs the masqueraded binary name with the article's verbatim launch command. Rationale: Triple-anchor on article-verbatim strings: (1) the binary name `.fullgc` (Code Block 1), (2) the absolute path `/ql/data/db/.fullgc` (Block snippet `b="/ql/data/db/.fullgc"`), and (3) the launch pattern `nohup "$b" >/dev/null 2>&1 &` (Block snippet). Filename was deliberately chosen to mimic JVM Full GC; the dot-prefix hides from `ls`; the path piggybacks on Qinglong's own data dir. Each anchor is high-fidelity on its own; combined they're near-zero FP. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/whyour/qinglong/issues/2923 • https://github.com/whyour/qinglong/issues/2928 • https://github.com/whyour/qinglong/issues/2926
ATT&CKT1059.004 T1496 T1036.005 T1564.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where (FileName == ".fullgc")
   or FolderPath endswith "/ql/data/db/.fullgc"
   or ProcessCommandLine has "/ql/data/db/.fullgc"
   or (InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("sh","bash","dash","nohup") and ProcessCommandLine matches regex @"(?i)nohup\s+[\"']?[^\s]*\.fullgc")
| extend OutputSuppressed = tostring(ProcessCommandLine) matches regex @"(?i)>\s*/dev/null\s+2>&1"
| extend Backgrounded = tostring(ProcessCommandLine) matches regex @"&\s*$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, FolderPath, ProcessCommandLine, SHA256, MD5, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessParentFileName, OutputSuppressed, Backgrounded
| order by Timestamp desc
// Primary: ASIM process events (Linux MDE, auditbeat, Sysmon-for-Linux normalised)
let AsimHits = ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where (ActingProcessName == ".fullgc")
   or ActingProcessCommandLine has "/ql/data/db/.fullgc"
   or (ParentProcessName in~ ("sh","bash","dash","nohup") and ActingProcessCommandLine matches regex @"(?i)nohup\s+[\"']?[^\s]*\.fullgc")
| extend OutputSuppressed = tostring(ActingProcessCommandLine) matches regex @"(?i)>\s*/dev/null\s+2>&1"
| extend Backgrounded = tostring(ActingProcessCommandLine) matches regex @"&\s*$"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine, SHA256, OutputSuppressed, Backgrounded;
// Secondary: raw Syslog auditd EXECVE for non-MDE Linux hosts
let SyslogHits = Syslog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where SyslogMessage has_any ("/ql/data/db/.fullgc"," .fullgc ")
| where SyslogMessage has_any ("EXECVE","execve","type=EXECVE","nohup")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname=Computer, ActorUsername="", ActingProcessName=".fullgc", ActingProcessCommandLine=SyslogMessage, ParentProcessName=ProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine="", SHA256="", OutputSuppressed=tostring(SyslogMessage matches regex @"(?i)>\s*/dev/null\s+2>&1"), Backgrounded=tostring(SyslogMessage matches regex @"&\s*$");
union AsimHits, SyslogHits
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Qinglong .fullgc Cryptominer Process Execution
id: 9d4b8e2f-6a1c-47d3-bc9f-2e8a4d6b1f53
description: Detects execution of the .fullgc cryptominer binary from /ql/data/db/, especially when launched via the article's verbatim nohup + suppressed-output + backgrounded pattern (`nohup "$b" >/dev/null 2>&1 &`). Filename masquerades as JVM Full GC.
references:
  - https://snyk.io/blog/qinglong-task-scheduler-rce-vulnerabilities/

source:linux.auditd @auditd.type:EXECVE (@process.executable.path:*\/ql\/data\/db\/\.fullgc OR @process.executable.path:*\/\.fullgc OR @process.command_line:*\/ql\/data\/db\/\.fullgc* OR @process.command_line:*nohup*\.fullgc*)
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2

| OutputSuppressed := if(regex(">\\s*/dev/null\\s+2>&1", field=CommandLine), then="yes", else="no")

// TVM tables are daily snapshots — pin a 1-day window so the engine

DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities

It's time to treat browser extensions like supply chain attack vectors

Aikido
2026-04-24 8 use cases 6 techniques 5 kill-chain phases detected

The Vercel breach followed a pattern the security industry knows well, where third-party code is implicitly trusted, then compromised upstream. We have a framework for that. We just haven't applied it to browser extensions yet. (Spoiler: We do this for software dependencies) Category: Vulnerabilities & Threats

ATT&CKT1176 T1190 T1195.002 T1528 T1555.003 T1566
Click any ATT&CK pill below to open it on the Matrix
Phase 1
Reconnaissance

Detected

Likely
Phase 7
Actions on Objectives
Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution · Email attachment opened from external sender
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Office app spawning script/LOLBin child process · Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → Suspicious browser extension installation
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking.
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs · Crypto-wallet file/keystore access by non-wallet process · OAuth consent / suspicious app grant

    - attack.t1555.003
    - attack.credential-access
logsource:
    category: file_access
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_path:
        TargetFilename|contains:
            - '\Google\Chrome\User Data\'
            - '\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\'
            - '\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\'
    selection_file:
        TargetFilename|endswith:
            - '\Login Data'
            - '\Cookies'
            - '\logins.json'
            - '\cookies.sqlite'
    filter_browser:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\chrome.exe'
            - '\msedge.exe'
            - '\firefox.exe'
            - '\brave.exe'
            - '\opera.exe'
    condition: selection_path and selection_file and not filter_browser
falsepositives:
    - Backup utilities reading user profile files
    - Browser sync agents from non-stock vendors
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
Crypto-wallet file/keystore access by non-wallet process Actions on Objectives High
Stealers / wallet drainers read keystore.json, MetaMask, Exodus, Atomic, Phantom data.
ATT&CKT1005
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem DeviceFileEvents
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where FolderPath has_any (@"\Ethereum\keystore\", @"\Bitcoin\", @"\Exodus\", @"\Electrum\wallets\", @"\MetaMask\", @"\Phantom\", @"\Atomic\Local Storage\")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("MetaMask.exe","Exodus.exe","Atomic.exe","electrum.exe","Bitcoin.exe","Phantom.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FolderPath, FileName, ActionType

ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where TargetFilePath has_any (@"\Ethereum\keystore\", @"\Bitcoin\",
                                  @"\Exodus\", @"\Electrum\wallets\",
                                  @"\MetaMask\", @"\Phantom\",
                                  @"\Atomic\Local Storage\")
| where ActingProcessName !in~ ("MetaMask.exe","Exodus.exe","Atomic.exe",
                                  "electrum.exe","Bitcoin.exe","Phantom.exe")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName,
          TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, EventType

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
Email attachment opened from external sender Delivery High
Attachment delivery + execution by recipient — most common malware initial access.
ATT&CKT1566.001 T1204.002
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Endpoint.Processes EmailAttachmentInfo DeviceProcessEvents
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MalAttachments = EmailAttachmentInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | project NetworkMessageId, RecipientEmailAddress,
              AttachmentFileName = FileName, AttachmentSHA256 = SHA256;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                      "mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
| join kind=inner MalAttachments on $left.AccountUpn == $right.RecipientEmailAddress
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, AttachmentFileName, AttachmentSHA256
// Sentinel doesn't have an attachment-hash table. Best approximation:
// OfficeActivity Send/Receive activity + correlate to host process spawn.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MailWithAttach = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation in~ ("Send","Receive")
    | where isnotempty(MessageId)
    | project EmailTime = TimeGenerated, MailboxOwnerUPN, Sender,
              Recipients, Subject, MessageId;
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "OUTLOOK.EXE"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count
    from datamodel=Email.All_Email
    where All_Email.file_name!="-"
    by All_Email.src_user, All_Email.recipient, All_Email.file_name, All_Email.subject
| rename All_Email.recipient as user
| join type=inner user
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
        from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
        where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
          AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
        by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
     | rename Processes.user as user]
| tstats summariesonly=false count
    from datamodel=Email.All_Email
    where All_Email.file_name!="-"
    by All_Email.src_user, All_Email.recipient, All_Email.file_name, All_Email.subject
| rename All_Email.recipient as user
| join type=inner user
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count
        from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
        where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
          AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
        by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
     | rename Processes.user as user]
Office app spawning script/LOLBin child process Exploitation High

| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine
SecurityEvent

      AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process

    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe","outlook.exe","onenote.exe","mspub.exe","visio.exe")
